purpose: What the pre-push hook judges, and what only CI judges. The hook is a fast local gate over the tree that is being pushed; CI is the authority over the whole tree. This file is the record of the difference — and scripts/check-hook-gates.py checks that the code still matches it, in both directions.

hook_scripts.declaration: PRE_PUSH_STEPS in scripts/src/sgate/gatekit/pre_push.py, and PRE_PUSH_SCRIPTS derived from it in scripts/src/sgate/commands/_registry.py
hook_scripts.why: one declaration serves the hook, the test fixture that drives it and this record — the hook reads the gates it runs instead of naming them, so a gate added to the declaration is a gate the hook runs, and a gate written into the hook is a gate nobody declared

ratchet.rule: A push must not make a gate redder than the base it starts from.
ratchet.base: the commit the branch forked from — the merge-base of the trunk and the pushed commit. SGATE_BASE_REF names it when the caller knows better; refs/remotes/<remote>/main, origin/main and main are the fallbacks.
ratchet.how: a gate that fails on the pushed tree is run again in the base tree, and the two answers are compared. What the base does not have, the push brought; what the base has as well is the trunk's finding. The gate suite's own tests are compared by their failing test ids, re-run one by one in the base tree.
ratchet.execution_status: The exit code of each run is part of what is compared, not only the text it printed. A run that failed without reporting anything broke rather than found something, and a broken run cannot say what the other tree has — so the comparison cannot be made, and a comparison that could not be made stops the push.
ratchet.what_it_is_not: The gate still reads the whole tree, on both sides. The ratchet decides whether a finding STOPS THE PUSH — it never decides whether the finding is there. CI still judges the whole tree, and the trunk's findings are the trunk's CI run to report.
ratchet.tool: scripts/pre-push-ratchet.py — a tool, not a gate: it judges nothing about the tree, it only compares two answers.
ratchet.no_base: a push with no base is judged as if everything in the tree were new — the safe direction.

detekt.judged_by_the_hook: the modules the pushed change can affect — computed from the module graph in scripts/changed-modules.py, never a list written here
detekt.partiality: The hook judges the modules the change can affect. CI judges every module the build declares that has a detekt verdict — the list is read from the build (`changed-modules.py --detekt-tasks`), not written out by hand, so a module added to the build is judged by CI on the next run. A violation in a module the change does not reach is CI's to find — so the local verdict is partial, and it says so instead of reading as full.

judged_by_ci_outside_the_module_graph.:pro:detekt: the source-available pro catalogue — a separate build that only exists with -PwithPro, so the module graph does not know it and the hook does not judge it. CI runs it in the pro job.

ktlint.judged_by_the_hook: the Kotlin sources the pushed commits carry — read merge-aware (`--diff-merges=first-parent`) and unescaped (`core.quotePath=false`), so a file a merge introduced and a path with non-ASCII letters are both in the scope; a push that carries no Kotlin source pays nothing for the formatting check
ktlint.judged_by_ci: every Kotlin source of the tree — `python3 scripts/ktlint-lint.py --require` in the `detekt` job
ktlint.partiality: The hook judges the Kotlin sources the push touches. CI judges every Kotlin source of the tree. A formatting defect in a file the push does not touch is CI's to find — so the local verdict is partial, and it says so instead of reading as full.

gate_suite.judged_by_the_hook: the test modules of the gate suite the push carries, that the pushed tree still holds — plus the modules that import a helper under `scripts/tests/` the push changes, and the modules those importers serve; run through `scripts/run-gate-tests.py --module`
gate_suite.judged_by_ci: every module of the gate suite — the `Gate tooling` job runs the whole suite
gate_suite.partiality: The hook judges the test modules the push touches. CI judges every module of the suite. A failure in a module the push does not carry is upstream's debt — it is red in CI, where the whole suite runs, and it is not this push's to carry. A push that touches no test of the suite pays nothing for it. A module the push deletes or renames away is not in the tree any more, so it is not judged: a name the tree does not hold is a name the runner turns into a failed test. A module that holds no test cases is not judged either: the runner answers NO TESTS RAN, which is the absence of a measurement, not a failure of the tree.

test_verdicts.not_judged_by_the_hook: The local verdict is a detekt verdict, and this module has no detekt task: it applies the plain kotlin("jvm") plugin. Its verdict is its test suite, CI runs it, and the local verdict says so instead of claiming a clean tree it never measured.
test_verdicts.why: Until 2026-10-23 this module was judged by nobody at all — not by CI, not by the hook, and not by the module graph, which carried a hand-written list of eight modules and did not read the build. The graph now reads settings.gradle.kts, so the module is known, and CI runs its tests.
